## (d) Extrapolation: trajectory and predicted next moves

1. **2022 – ELK/alignment blogging and theory:** "If you're very optimistic about ELK…" (solo, 2022).
2. **2023–2024 – Representation and circuit interpretability:** *The Geometry of Truth*; *Sparse Feature Circuits*.
3. **2024 – Behaviorally identical models, cognition-based oversight:** *Discriminating Behaviorally Identical Classifiers*. 
  > "In brief, cognition-based oversight aims to evaluate models according to whether they’re performing intended cognition, instead of whether they have intended input/output behavior."  
  > -- `research__discriminating_behaviorally_identical_classifiers__c8a32435` (2024-04-18; solo author) 
  > "Instead of asking how to improve the existing approaches to scalable oversight, I’m going to take a different tack: **I will impose the pessimistic assumption that our models are effectively** ***behaviorally identical***"  
  > -- `research__discriminating_behaviorally_identical_classifiers__c8a32435` (2024-04-18; solo author)
4. **2025 H1 – Auditing for hidden objectives, validating interpretability downstream:** *Auditing language models for hidden objectives*; *Downstream applications…* 
  > "We risk inadvertently deploying AIs that are “right for the wrong reasons,” showing us what we want to see while knowingly violating our intent."  
  > -- `research__auditing_language_models_for_hidden_objectives_ccb192d2` (2025-03-13; first author) 
  > "I think that if your insights allow you to do something that no one else is able to do—i.e. to outperform baselines on a downstream task—then they're less likely to be illusory or unimportant."  
  > -- `research__downstream_applications_as_validation_of_interpret_e67e7613` (2025-03-31; solo author)
5. **2025 H2 – Auditing agents, belief editing, eval-awareness, Petri:** *Building and evaluating alignment auditing agents*; *Steering Evaluation-Aware Language Models…*; *Petri*. 
  > "Petri enables researchers to test hypotheses about model behavior in minutes, using AI agents to explore target models across realistic multi-turn scenarios."  
  > -- `research__petri_an_open_source_auditing_tool_to_accelerate_a_e6740f00` (2025-10-07; solo author) 
  > "By training a model organism, we know the model’s intended behaviors in evaluation and in deployment. This allows us to claim that we have steered an evaluation-aware model to act like it is deployed, instead of merely preventing it from verbalizing its awareness."  
  > -- `research__steering_evaluation_aware_language_models_to_act_l_3180f0ad` (2025-10-23; middle author)
6. **Late 2025–2026 – Testbeds, lie detection, sandbagging, persona theory:** *Auditing Games for Sandbagging*; *The persona selection model*; *AuditBench*. 
  > "After instilling a particular behavior into a target model, we find that they often readily confess their hidden behaviors when directly asked. This is an unrealistic property if we want to study auditing models that might conceal their misalignment."  
  > -- `research__auditbench_evaluating_alignment_auditing_technique_b35d8430` (2026-02-26; middle author) 
  > "PSM does not assert the Assistant is a single, coherent persona that is consistent across contexts. Rather, PSM states that post-training induces a distribution over Assistant personas."  
  > -- `research__the_persona_selection_model_8a0e511f` (2026-02-23; solo author)
7. **2026 – Self-explanation and in-the-wild behavior:** *Training Models to Predict and Explain Their In-the-Wild Behavior*. 
  > "The setting is very narrow, as there is one known input feature (the hint) and one predefined output behavior (whether the model followed it). The questions we actually want self-explanations to answer in deployment"  
  > -- `research__training_models_to_predict_and_explain_their_in_th_bfc9031b` (2026-09-04; last author) 
  > "The counterfactual outcome labels are also cheap and objective to verify, because the label of a counterfactual claim comes from actually re-running the model under the intervention and checking whether the behavior rate moved."  
  > -- `research__training_models_to_predict_and_explain_their_in_th_bfc9031b` (2026-09-04; last author)

**Predicted next moves** (predictions)
- Honeypot-realism search with steered on-policy targets and an investigator model. Chain: eval-awareness work leads to 
  > "Steering can help speed up this search for more realistic honeypot environments: we first use our steered-to-deployment model to generate outputs in our honeypot environment. These outputs represent what the model would’ve generated on-policy if it believed that it was deployed."  
  > -- `research__steering_evaluation_aware_language_models_to_act_l_3180f0ad` (2025-10-23; middle author).
- Better non-CoT measures of eval-relevant belief. 
  > "We should also develop more methods for measuring the model’s evaluation-relevant beliefs beyond reading its chain of thought (Needham et al., 2025), which could allow us to iterate and create better steering methods"  
  > -- `research__steering_evaluation_aware_language_models_to_act_l_3180f0ad` (2025-10-23; middle author)
- Harder testbeds with strategic, coherent deception and more realistic model organisms (e.g. via synthetic documents). 
  > "Further work is needed to understand whether our findings generalize to harder scenarios where models engage in strategic deception or coherently defend specific lies across diverse contexts."  
  > -- `research__evaluating_honesty_and_lie_detection_techniques_on_682cb3e4` (2025-11-25; middle author) 
  > "For future investigations, model organisms could be created using synthetic document fine tuning to investigate whether they can engage in undetectable sandbagging without the aid of a directly internalized policy"  
  > -- `research__auditing_games_for_sandbagging_db746163` (2025-12-08; middle author)
- Testbeds on naturally occurring issues, e.g. already-deployed models. 
  > "One possibility here is to use target models which have already been commercially deployed, and use the set of issues discovered in deployment as a ground truth for an auditing agent."  
  > -- `research__towards_alignment_auditing_as_a_numbers_go_up_scie_25f004d5` (2025-08-04; solo author) 
  > "To make sure that techniques are being tested in an apples-to-apples way, it would be nice to have open-source implementations of auditing agents and test environments."  
  > -- `research__towards_alignment_auditing_as_a_numbers_go_up_scie_25f004d5` (2025-08-04; solo author)
- RL against counterfactual simulatability and held-out-task generalization. 
  > "We think datasets such as ours are a promising testbed for future self-explanation methods (a natural direction is to directly RL against the counterfactual simulatability metric)."  
  > -- `research__training_models_to_predict_and_explain_their_in_th_bfc9031b` (2026-09-04; last author) 
  > "To our knowledge, no training for causal self-explanations has been shown to generalize to a genuinely held-out task. Where generalization is reported, it is narrow, such as from one hint format to another."  
  > -- `research__training_models_to_predict_and_explain_their_in_th_bfc9031b` (2026-09-04; last author)
- More diverse Petri seeds to extend beyond the narrow defaults. 
  > "its effectiveness is limited by the use of the default seed instructions, which focus on a fairly narrow set of scenarios, largely involving high-stakes sabotage opportunities, and which were not designed to cover the full range of potentially concerning behaviors out of the box."  
  > -- `research__auditbench_evaluating_alignment_auditing_technique_b35d8430` (2026-02-26; middle author)
